resources.string: Hold volume down at the lowest media volume to zoom into 10 finer steps.

Volume Zoom watches only the volume keys. When media is at its lowest audible step, hold volume down to zoom into 10 extra, quieter steps (software attenuation of the media output). Volume up steps back out. No other input or screen content is read.
Volume Zoom is off. In Accessibility → Volume Zoom, turn on \"Use Volume Zoom\". Leave \"Volume Zoom shortcut\" off: it only adds a floating button, and the volume keys work without it.

If Android says \"App was denied access\" when you turn it on: open App info, tap ⋮ (top right), choose \"Allow restricted settings\" and turn it on again. Android only shows that option after it has blocked the switch once. It applies to apps installed from a file, not to ones from an app store such as F-Droid.

Lower media volume to its last step, then hold volume down to zoom in (starts at 0 dB). Each down press is one fine step quieter, and up steps back out. A fresh press on the last fine step mutes. A quick press at the last step still mutes as usual.
Deepest fine step: −%1$d dB (%2$.1f dB per step)
Hold time to zoom in: %1$d ms
Volume keys control media when nothing is playing (Pixel default; turn off if idle keys change the ringer)
